body.statement: For every \(s\in[1,2]\) and \(M\ge2\), there exists \(C_{\mathrm{sep}}=C_{\mathrm{sep}}(s,M)>0\), independent of \(n\), \(P\), \(c\), \(\vartheta\), and every conditional treatment--outcome association, such that for every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and \(c\in[1/4,3/4]\), \[\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\left\{\mathcal L_P(c,\vartheta)-\mathcal L_P(c_P,\theta_P)\right\}\ge C_{\mathrm{sep}}\kappa_n^2\min\{|c-c_P|,h_n\}.\] Here \(\mathcal L_P\) is the four-cell Bernoulli-pair loss in \(\text{def:population-profile-loss}\), its optimization runs over all \(q\in\mathcal Q(c,\vartheta)\), the reference split is \((c_P,\theta_P)\), and its extended-real convention covers zero and singular cells.
body.justification: The deterministic profile gap is the first proof step that the refuted moving-window localizer lacked.
body.gap: Porter and Yu (2015) and Tuvaandorj (2020) analyze unknown sharp-RD locations, but do not establish this support-wide false-split gap for a vanishing binary first stage under separate one-sided H\"older constraints.
body.consumer: The bound converts global cutoff profiling from a heuristic into a certifiable localization device before stochastic calibration is attempted.
